page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It lacks local storage and dedicated GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by stress-ng single-core CPU tests and poor single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression results. However, the instance demonstrates average multi-core performance across stress-ng multi-core, Passmark CPU, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression tests. Memory bandwidth is also average, reaching 655.24 GB/sec for cached reads and approximately 77.7 GB/sec for uncached reads.

Given its hardware profile, the ecs.sn2ne.4xlarge offers a cost-efficient option for workloads that can leverage multi-threaded execution rather than single-core speed. It is well-suited for static web serving, Redis caching, and database operations, where it achieves average performance metrics. It is less suitable for single-threaded tasks or medium-to-large language model inference, where performance drops to weak levels.

Operating on the KVM hypervisor, this x86_64 instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. Performance benchmarks indicate a notable tradeoff: single-core CPU execution and single-threaded compression tasks are weak, while multi-core operations, memory bandwidth, and database operations perform at average levels. Consequently, this instance is best suited for multi-threaded workloads, static web serving, Redis caching, and general-purpose database applications that do not require high single-thread performance.
